 By Chris Lea, WRAL-TV sports anchor/reporter
 With two games remaining in the regular season, the North Carolina Courage are running out of time to secure a spot in the NWSL postseason.
 The Courage visit the Portland Thorns on Friday in a crucial road matchup, knowing they need points to keep their playoff hopes alive. The Courage have 42 points and sit ninth in the table, one point behind Seattle and two behind Portland. The top eight teams make the playoffs. 
 Other WRAL Top Stories
 Kickoff is at 10 p.m.
 “We need to perform and need to take points to make sure we do the playoff,” head coach Mak Lind said. “Exciting times!”
 A North Carolina win against Portland means the Courage can clinch a spot in the playoffs with a win in the season-finale against Denver on Nov. 1. If the Courage lose and Seattle (43 points) wins this week, North Carolina would be eliminated from playoff contention. 
 North Carolina missed the playoffs by a single point last season. 
 The Courage enter the final stretch of the season believing they have built the foundation to compete for a championship. Lind said the team’s challenge now is executing when it matters most.
 “We just have to take it, and I believe we have so much foundation,” Lind said. “We just have to take it. And when I say take it, I mean go out and perform and win the game.”
 Left wing Ashley Sanchez has a league-high 20 goals, tied for the NWSL single-season record. Sanchez has gone two games without a goal. Only once this season has she gone three games without scoring. Portland star Sophia Wilson is third in the league with 13 goals, but she will miss Friday night's game related to a red card.
 Forward Hannah Betfort said the team is prepared for the pressure of the postseason race, especially in a league where the standings have remained tight throughout the season.
 “This year, it does feel like there’s a little bit more of an edge, more of a hunger to get there,” Betfort said. “We’ve been performing well. Like now’s the time to seal that off and make sure that we get into the postseason.”
 The Courage will face a difficult test in Portland, where the Thorns have a strong home atmosphere. North Carolina has not won in Portland since 2019, adding another challenge to an already important matchup.
 Lind said the team has made adjustments for the season’s final games, including implementing a strategy called “Code Red” to create more urgency when a result is needed.
 The Courage will look to maintain their identity while finding ways to generate scoring opportunities and earn valuable points on the road.
